correctness.rationale: Definitions and conditional expectation were reconstructed from priority and student-permutation quantifiers. The identity E[JE|priority,order]=sum school-wise Kendall distances/4 follows by uniformity of each assigned school and linearity, and is independently checked on a nontrivial profile over all 24 common preferences. Every 24^4 priority quadruple and 24 serial orders are visited by C++17 exact-integer loops, with expected counts and checksum asserted; the independent NumPy pairwise-majority implementation reproduces all 13 score and nine minimizer multiplicity frequencies. A direct adjacent-transposition argument proves K=12 exactly when all six student pairs split the schools 2–2; random-order mean 3 follows from pairwise symmetry. The computation proves only this finite population; no infinite generalization is inferred.

value.rationale: The literature motivates minimizing justified envy while preserving the strategic and Pareto properties of serial dictatorship, but the expected size of the gain and prevalence of optimal-order ties under a transparent baseline are not answered by the general mechanism theorem. The complete natural 4-school priority census gives an exact 37.49% average expected improvement, a very rare pairwise-balanced no-benefit configuration (11/1536), and an 84.57% non-uniqueness rate relevant to tie-breaking. Four students and four schools form a small but nontrivial independent-priority benchmark; the invariant is defined by the mechanism design objective rather than an arbitrary subcase.
